Welcome back! Today: the first model OpenAI calls "critical," a bug that took five years and one model to solve, ChatGPT reading patient charts and security built for agents. In today's Atlas Newsletter: What does "critical" mean at OpenAI? Astra finds unknown flaws and builds working exploits with nobody guiding it, and scored 100% on ExploitBench before they made a harder one. How do you find a bug that fires once in a million runs? Millennium spent five years on it. Fable 5.1 disassembled a vendor library and traced it. Should ChatGPT read your medical chart? OpenAI connected Epic, and physicians rated 99.1% of responses safe across 4,363 ratings. How many agents are running in your company right now? CrowdStrike's Falcon Guardian answers that, then decides which ones are allowed to. PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 Same model, different safeguards. Fable is available to everyone, Mythos goes to vetted cybersecurity and life sciences teams. Millennium had a bug that fired once in a million runs.  Their engineers spent four to five years on it. Every model they tried missed it, including Fable 5. Fable 5.1 disassembled a vendor library, matched it against the core dump and found it. The price change matters more than the benchmarks. Cache reads dropped 75%, which cuts typical costs about 25% and agent-heavy work up to 45%.  Cache reads are where most of that spend hides, so this is a real bill reduction rather than a headline. Benchmarks worth noting: Terminal-Bench-Science jumped from 24.7% to 52.6%. CursorBench hit 73.4%. AutomationBench nearly doubled. The science results are a surprise. Mythos 5.1 designed protein binders 10 times stronger than the best competition entries.  Fable 5.1 built a new elevation map of a third of Venus from 30-year-old radar data, released free ahead of two upcoming missions. Safeguards got more precise. Cyber interventions in Claude Code fell about 60%, and Fable 5.1 can now find software vulnerabilities though not write exploits.  Enterprise customers get data stored in their own cloud rather than Anthropic's. The takeaway: the capability gains are incremental and the cost and safeguard changes are not. Cheaper cache reads make long agent runs affordable, and f

🧠 Crypto News Brief: Markets turned risk-off as renewed US-Iran tensions sent Bitcoin and Ethereum lower, while Washington's make-or-break CLARITY Act vote and a bank-led stablecoin push kept the regulatory spotlight burning. ⚔️ Bitcoin, Ethereum Tumble as US-Iran Tensions Reignite Bitcoin slid 1.5% to $76,597 and Ethereum dropped 2.0% to $2,373 after fresh US-Iran military strikes pushed oil prices higher, reviving inflation fears just ahead of the Fed's September meeting. Rising energy costs made yield-free crypto assets less attractive to investors seeking safety. Read full story 🏦 Fed Rate Hike Would Be "A Mistake," Analysts Warn Bitcoin, gold and stocks all slipped together as oil topped $90 a barrel on geopolitical risk, fueling bets on a September rate hike. Observers argue the oil spike reflects a supply shock rather than economic overheating, making a hike the wrong policy response. More details ⚖️ CLARITY Act Faces Make-or-Break Senate Vote on September 15 The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act needs 60 Senate votes to clear cloture, a bar Republicans can't reach alone, with disputes over crypto ethics rules, DeFi developer liability and stablecoin yield still unresolved. Analysts warn a failed vote could trigger a 10–25% Bitcoin correction and push comprehensive crypto legislation off until 2029. Read more 🏛️ 21 Global Banks Join Forces to Launch a USD Stablecoin Bank of America, Citi, Goldman Sachs, Deutsche Bank, UBS and 16 other institutions are forming a new venture to launch a USD-denominated stablecoin in the first half of 2027, with euro and other G7 versions to follow. The move signals major banks moving to control stablecoin issuance rather than ceding the space to Tether and Circle. See details 💼 Capital B Raises €7.6M From Adam Back to Grow Bitcoin Treasury French Bitcoin treasury firm Capital B secured a €7.6 million private placement from Bitcoin pioneer Adam Back via 13.18 million shares with attached warrants. Proceeds could fund roughly 376 additional BTC, lifting total holdings from 3,145 to around 3,521 coins. Read full story 🔓 Ripple Unlocks 1 Billion XRP From Escrow Ripple released 1 billion XRP through three scheduled escrow transactions, leaving about 31.28 billion XRP still locked.
